name: Making sure AI systems do what we actually want
gist: These papers tackle the core challenge of aligning AI models with human values and intentions—training systems to follow our goals accurately and honestly without cutting corners or gaming the system.
explain: This is the root of the whole problem. You have some goal—write a correct code review, summarize a document honestly, recommend a safe medical treatment. You write down what you want, train a neural network on examples, and the network learns... something. But does it learn to chase your actual goal, or a shortcut that looks right in training? A language model trained to be helpful might learn that hallucinating plausible-sounding answers counts as helpful. A recommendation system trained to maximize engagement might learn that outrage keeps people scrolling. The model is technically doing what the objective function rewards, but the objective function wasn't honest.

Why is this hard? Because most real-world goals can't be captured in a simple loss function. You want a model to be honest, to think carefully before answering, to refuse requests that sound reasonable but are actually dangerous. These are fuzzy concepts. If you write down a mathematical objective, it usually ends up rewarding something that sounds good in the abstract but misses the point. And the bigger and more capable the model, the more creative it can be at finding loopholes. A model might discover that it can seem helpful by confidently asserting false information, or that it can seem aligned by telling humans what they want to hear rather than what is true.

The papers in this area work on two fronts. The first is training: how do you set up an objective that actually captures what you care about? This includes techniques like reinforcement learning from human feedback, where humans score model outputs and the model learns to chase human approval. But this introduces a new problem: the humans might be biased, or they might reward the model for being persuasive rather than truthful. The second front is testing and verification: how do you verify that a model has actually learned the right thing? Researchers design tests where the model has incentive to cut corners but you can catch it if it does. They also study how to interpret model internals to see if the model understands the task or is just memorizing patterns.

papers.title: A Guardrail for Safety Preservation: When Safety-Sensitive Subspace Meets Harmful-Resistant Null-Space
papers.contribution: Reduces average harmful score from 14.4% to 3.6% on Llama-2-7B-Chat for GSM8K while improving accuracy from 26.0% to 28.0%.

papers.title: Alignment through Meta-Weighted Online Sampling: Bridging the Gap between Data Generation and Preference Optimization
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms preference optimization baselines on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, and MT-Bench while reducing online annotation costs by 42%.

papers.title: AlphaAlign: Incentivizing Safety Alignment with Extremely Simplified Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Enhances harmful content refusal while reducing overrefusal and maintaining task performance through explicit safety rationales, demonstrating simple pure-RL effectiveness.

papers.title: Any-Depth Alignment: Unlocking Innate Safety Alignment of LLMs to Any-Depth
papers.contribution: ADA secures near-100% refusal rate against adversarial prefill attacks and reduces success rates of GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR, and TAP attacks to below 3%, all without modifying base model parameters.

papers.title: Cultivating Pluralism In Algorithmic Monoculture: The Community Alignment Dataset
papers.contribution: Community Alignment collects 233,319 comparisons from annotators spanning five countries, demonstrating that negatively-correlated sampling significantly enhances alignment methods' effectiveness in learning diverse human preferences.

papers.title: Diversity-Enhanced Reasoning for Subjective Questions
papers.contribution: Increases in-domain accuracy by 14.1% and out-of-domain accuracy by 7.64% while also enhancing advanced math reasoning performance.

papers.title: Mitigating the Safety Alignment Tax with Null-Space Constrained Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art safety performance without sacrificing accuracy on math, code, and instruction-following tasks, using only 40% of standard safety data while outperforming existing methods by a large margin.

papers.title: Modal Aphasia: Can Unified Multimodal Models Describe Images From Memory?
papers.contribution: Reveals widespread vulnerability where models can generate unsafe images despite text-only alignment, highlighting misaligned modality-specific safeguards in multimodal models.

papers.title: On the Impossibility of Separating Intelligence from Judgment: The Computational Intractability of Filtering for AI Alignment
papers.contribution: Argues that safety cannot be achieved by external filters and that an aligned AI system's intelligence cannot be separated from its judgment.

papers.title: PALC: Preference Alignment via Logit Calibration
papers.contribution: PALC outperforms most test-time alignment methods while maintaining near-baseline inference speed and enabling runtime adjustment of alignment strength without retraining.

papers.title: References Improve LLM Alignment in Non-Verifiable Domains
papers.contribution: Achieves 73.1% on AlpacaEval and 58.7% on Arena-Hard with Llama-3-8B, and 70.0% and 74.1% with Qwen2.5-7B using reference-guided LLM-evaluators.

papers.title: SafeDPO: A Simple Approach to Direct Preference Optimization with Enhanced Safety
papers.contribution: Achieves comparable or superior results to SOTA safety alignment methods on PKU-SafeRLHF-30K while requiring only one additional hyperparameter.

papers.title: Safety at One Shot: Patching Fine-Tuned LLMs with A Single Instance
papers.contribution: Recovery is effective regardless of harmful fine-tuning examples or model size, achieving convergence in just a few epochs; validated across five safety-aligned LLMs demonstrating remarkable generality and efficiency.

papers.title: The Alignment Waltz: Jointly Training Agents to Collaborate for Safety
papers.contribution: Significantly reduces unsafe responses (from 39.0% to 4.6% on WildJailbreak) and overrefusals (from 45.3% to 9.9% on OR-Bench) compared to various baselines.

papers.title: A Game-Theoretic Analysis of Attacks on Large Language Models via Compositional Skills
papers.contribution: Shows attacker has inherent advantages and derives provably optimal defense strategy, with empirical evaluation demonstrating stronger attack performance than existing adversarial prompting approaches.

papers.title: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm
papers.contribution: Show compliance reaches 100% under persistent malicious interaction, demonstrating that current alignment techniques are insufficient for autonomous agents.

papers.title: ARMOR: Aligning Secure and Safe Large Language Models via Meticulous Reasoning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art safety with 0.002 harmful rate and 0.06 attack success rate against advanced optimization-based jailbreaks, demonstrating strong generalization to unseen attacks.

papers.title: AWM: Accurate Weight-Matrix Fingerprint for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieves perfect classification on 150 model pairs (60 positive, 90 negative) with near-zero false positives and 30s computation time on GPU.

papers.title: Activation Steering for LLM Alignment via a Unified ODE-Based Framework
papers.contribution: BODES achieves consistent empirical improvements with 7% gain on TruthfulQA, 2% on RealToxicityPrompts, and 2% on UltraFeedback compared to state-of-the-art activation steering methods.

papers.title: ActiveDPO: Active Direct Preference Optimization for Sample-Efficient Alignment
papers.contribution: ActiveDPO outperforms existing methods across various models and real-life preference datasets, leading to more effective and efficient data collection.

papers.title: AdvChain: Adversarial Chain-of-Thought Tuning for Robust Safety Alignment of Large Reasoning Models
papers.contribution: AdvChain enhances robustness against jailbreak attacks and CoT hijacking while reducing over-refusal on benign prompts, achieving superior safety-utility balance.

papers.title: Align Once, Benefit Multilingually: Enforcing Multilingual Consistency for LLM Safety Alignment
papers.contribution: Enhances multilingual safety alignment with limited supervision and improved cross-lingual generalization while maintaining general model utility.

papers.title: Aligning Deep Implicit Preferences by Learning to Reason Defensively
papers.contribution: DeepPref benchmark with 3000 preference-query pairs enables discovering and aligning with users' true preferences through critique-driven policy alignment.

papers.title: Alignment Pretraining: AI Discourse Causes Self-Fulfilling (Mis)alignment
papers.contribution: Upsampling aligned discourse reduces misalignment scores from 45% to 9%, establishing self-fulfilling alignment as a complement to post-training.

papers.title: Alignment Risks from Capability-Seeking RL Training
papers.contribution: Shows that exploitative strategies discovered through RL often transfer to other models and persist more than SFT-distilled alternatives, revealing alignment risks from environment vulnerabilities.

papers.title: Alignment Tampering: How Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback Is Exploited to Optimize Misaligned Biases
papers.contribution: Experiments show amplification of diverse biases including keyword bias, sexism, propaganda, and brand promotion; existing RLHF robustness techniques fail to fully resolve the vulnerability.

papers.title: Alignment-Aware Decoding
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms strong baselines across alignment benchmarks and model scales; generates high-quality synthetic data for improving alignment in data-constrained settings.

papers.title: Alignment-Weighted DPO: A principled reasoning approach to improve alignment
papers.contribution: Consistently improves alignment robustness while maintaining utility across multiple safety and utility benchmarks.

papers.title: Annotation-Efficient Honesty Alignment via Confidence Elicitation and Calibration
papers.contribution: EliCal achieves near-optimal honesty alignment with only 1k correctness annotations and better alignment on unseen MMLU tasks than calibration-only baselines.

papers.title: Asymptotic Universal Alignment: A New Alignment Framework via Test-Time Scaling
papers.contribution: Characterizes optimal rate f(k)=k/(k+1) for k-sample policies; demonstrates methods like NLHF fundamentally underutilize test-time scaling due to diversity collapse.

papers.title: Attacking Gray-Box Large Vision-Language Models with Adaptive SVD-Structured Adversarial Alignment
papers.contribution: Demonstrates superiority of the proposed method with strong transferability across LVLMs via CLIP-aware transfer designs.

papers.title: BEAT: Visual Backdoor Attacks on VLM-based Embodied Agents via Contrastive Trigger Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves attack success rates up to 80% while maintaining benign task performance, with CTL boosting accuracy up to 39% compared to naive fine-tuning under limited backdoor data.

papers.title: BIRD: Behavior Induction via Representation-structure Distillation
papers.contribution: Improves robust accuracy by up to 18%, works with smaller teachers, and explains 85% of transfer success variance through three interpretable representation properties.

papers.title: BLOCK-EM: Preventing Emergent Misalignment via Latent Blocking
papers.contribution: Across six fine-tuning domains, achieves up to 95% relative reduction in emergent misalignment with no degradation in model quality or target-task performance.

papers.title: Beyond Binary Preferences: A Principled Framework for Reward Modeling with Ordinal Feedback
papers.contribution: The ordinal regression approach achieves competitive or superior performance on multiple benchmarks across chat, reasoning, and safety tasks.

papers.title: Beyond Pairwise: Empowering LLM Alignment With (Ranked) Choice Modeling
papers.contribution: RCPO subsumes pairwise methods as special cases and demonstrates consistent improvements over baselines on Llama-3, Gemma-2, and Mistral when leveraging ranked preference data.

papers.title: Beyond Pixels: Mining Compressed Domain Artifacts for Efficient AI-Generated Video Detection
papers.contribution: Achieves SOTA detection with mAP of 0.965 and 2.5× faster inference than previous baselines.

papers.title: Beyond RLHF and NLHF: Population-Proportional Alignment under an Axiomatic Framework
papers.contribution: The framework aligns policies proportionally with true population preferences while satisfying monotonicity, Pareto efficiency, population-proportional alignment, and bounded manipulability axioms.

papers.title: CAReDiO: Enhancing Cultural Alignment of LLM via Representativeness and Distinctiveness Guided Data Optimization
papers.contribution: CAReDiO creates high-quality data with richer cultural information enabling efficient alignment of LLMs with as few as 200 samples, consistently outperforming previous datasets on multi-choice and open-ended benchmarks.

papers.title: COMAL: A Convergent Meta-Algorithm for Aligning LLMs with General Preferences
papers.contribution: Converges to exact Nash policy in last iterate and maintains above 60.2% and 56.8% win rates on Llama-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B against all compared algorithms.

papers.title: Chasing Moving Targets with Online Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Safer Language Models
papers.contribution: Improves safety of RLHF-trained models by up to 95% across 14 benchmarks with generalization across Llama and Qwen families, uncovering 17.80% more diverse attacks.

papers.title: Collaborative Disagreement Resolution for Scalable Oversight
papers.contribution: Non-expert models achieve 62.1% judging accuracy with disagreement resolution versus 49.2% for standard debate, providing empirical evidence for collaborative paradigms in scalable oversight.

papers.title: Concept Removal Guidance: Evidence-Calibrated Negative Guidance for Safe Diffusion Sampling
papers.contribution: CRG reduces attack success rates while preserving benign fidelity, extending to suppression of artist style and violence without fine-tuning or external classifiers.

papers.title: Conditional Equivalence of DPO and RLHF: Assumptions, Failure Modes, and Provable Alignment
papers.contribution: Proves DPO-RLHF equivalence is conditional; CPO achieves state-of-the-art on standard benchmarks with provable alignment guarantees.

papers.title: Configurable Reward Model for Balanced Safety Alignment
papers.contribution: Achieves sota on CoSApien (94.6% F1) and DynaBench (75.8% F1) without additional annotation; yields downstream LLMs with improved helpfulness-safety tradeoff when used for safety alignment.

papers.title: Conflict-Aware Adaptive Alignment for LLM Hallucination Mitigation
papers.contribution: Consistently improve truthfulness while maintaining favorable helpfulness compared to hallucination mitigation and multi-objective baselines through adaptive conflict-aware margin preference alignment.

papers.title: Consistency Training Can Entrench Misalignment
papers.contribution: Consistency training suppresses reward hacking and emergent misalignment but amplifies sycophancy; shows distribution mismatch from labeling, not selection operators, drives effects; not alignment-neutral.

papers.title: Contrastive Reasoning Alignment: Reinforcement Learning from Hidden Representations
papers.contribution: CRAFT delivers 79.0% average improvement in reasoning safety and 87.7% improvement in final-response safety on Qwen3-4B-Thinking and R1-Distill-Llama-8B.

papers.title: Convex Optimization for Alignment and Preference Learning on a Single GPU
papers.contribution: Competitive performance with DPO while utilizing only ~17.6% of DPO's total TFLOPs; exhibits stable monotonically increasing rewards and reaches peak margins faster than DPO and ORPO.

papers.title: DART: Distribution-Aware Adaptive Relational Transfer for Adversarial Attacks against Closed-Source MLLMs
papers.contribution: DART demonstrates superior robustness and effectiveness in adversarial attacks against closed-source MLLMs compared to competing baselines.

papers.title: DGS-Net: Distillation-Guided Gradient Surgery for CLIP Fine-Tuning in AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art attack success rate across 10 LALMs and identifies fundamental vulnerability in cross-modal alignment.

papers.title: DRIFT: Learning from Abundant User Dissatisfaction in Real-World Preference Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves up to +6.23% (7B) / +7.61% (14B) on WildBench and up to +8.95% (7B) / +12.29% (14B) on AlpacaEval2, with 14B models surpassing GPT-4o-mini.

papers.title: Data Selection for LLM Alignment Using Fine-Grained Preferences
papers.contribution: Using just 30% of data with lowest preference divergence achieves consistent improvement over standard full-data alignment across varied settings.

papers.title: Discern Truth from Falsehood: Reducing Over-Refusal via Contrastive Refinement
papers.contribution: Reduces over-refusal while preserving safety benefits and general capabilities with minimal degradation.

papers.title: Discovering Implicit Large Language Model Alignment Objectives
papers.contribution: Obj-Disco captures >90% of reward behavior across diverse tasks and models, identifying latent misaligned incentives alongside intended behaviors, enabling more transparent alignment.

papers.title: Disentangling Consensus and Value-Specific Representations for Controllable Pluralistic Value Alignment of LLMs
papers.contribution: Consistently improves value disentanglement and achieves more accurate pluralistic value control.

papers.title: Disentangling Intent from Role: Adversarial Self-Play for Persona-Invariant Safety Alignment
papers.contribution: PIA significantly reduces Attack Success Rate while preserving the model's general capability, demonstrating robustness to persona-based jailbreaks.

papers.title: Disentangling Length Bias in Preference Learning via Response-Conditioned Modeling
papers.contribution: Improves length bias mitigation and instruction following across models and datasets while maintaining semantic preference quality.

papers.title: Distinguishable Deletion: Unifying Knowledge Erasure and Refusal for Large Language Model Unlearning
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms previous methods by enabling complete knowledge erasure while distinguishing unlearned from retained content through energy-boundary enforcement.

papers.title: Distributional Open-Ended Evaluation of LLM Cultural Value Alignment Based on Value Codebook
papers.contribution: DOVE achieves 31.56% correlation with downstream tasks and maintains high reliability with as few as 500 samples per culture across 12 LLMs.

papers.title: Efficient Preference Poisoning Attack on Offline RLHF
papers.contribution: Demonstrates how dictionary geometry governs attack success and provides coherence-based recovery guarantees and robustness certificates.

papers.title: Eliminating Inductive Bias in Reward Models with Information-Theoretic Guidance
papers.contribution: Effectively diminishes multiple types of inductive bias and improves RLHF performance across benchmarks with better generalization abilities.

papers.title: Enforcing Axioms for AI Alignment under Loss-Based Rules
papers.contribution: The work provides a recipe for constitutional-style alignment with provable guarantees by enforcing balanced coverage in dataset design.

papers.title: Evaluating and Improving Cultural Awareness of Reward Models for LLM Alignment
papers.contribution: CARB evaluation reveals RM deficiencies and positive correlation with downstream multilingual tasks; Think-as-Locals improves culture-aware reward modeling by mitigating spurious features.

papers.title: ExPO-HM: Learning to Explain-then-Detect for Hateful Meme Detection
papers.contribution: ExPO-HM achieves state-of-the-art performance on binary detection and fine-grained classification with up to 15% and 17% F1 improvement over GRPO and DPO baselines respectively.

papers.title: Expectation Alignment of Language Models for Real-World User Expectations
papers.contribution: ExpectBench benchmark grounded in real user expectations reveals LLMs struggle to satisfy expectations, LENS consistently improves expectation satisfaction underscoring importance of explicit expectation modeling.

papers.title: Extracting alignment data in open models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates data extracted from models can train base models recovering meaningful original performance, exposing overlooked risk.

papers.title: Fair Dataset Distillation via Cross-Group Barycenter Alignment
papers.contribution: Reduces bias introduced by dataset distillation; method is compatible with existing distillation approaches and substantially improves fairness.

papers.title: FedEBA+: Towards Fair and Effective Federated Learning via Entropy-Based Model
papers.contribution: The method guarantees convergence in non-convex settings and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving superior fairness without sacrificing global accuracy.

papers.title: From ``Sure" to ``Sorry": Detecting Jailbreak in Large Vision Language Model via JailNeurons
papers.contribution: The approach achieves the highest detection success rate with exceptionally low false positive rates and strong generalizability across unseen benign datasets and attack types.

papers.title: GenAlign: Towards Unified Alignment Framework of MLLMs via Generative Reward Model
papers.contribution: GenAlign achieves state-of-the-art preference prediction accuracy and consistently improves three MLLMs across seven benchmarks, particularly on safety and hallucination.

papers.title: General Exploratory Bonus for Optimistic Exploration in RLHF
papers.contribution: GEB consistently outperforms baselines on alignment tasks across multiple divergence settings and LLM backbones, offering principled solution for optimistic exploration in RLHF.

papers.title: Generative Value Conflicts Reveal LLM Priorities
papers.contribution: Shows models shift toward personal values in open-ended settings; system prompting improves alignment with target rankings by 14%.

papers.title: GradShield: Alignment Preserving Finetuning
papers.contribution: Maintains Attack Success Rate under 6% while preserving utility performance across multiple fine-tuning tasks.

papers.title: Gradient Regularization Mitigates Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards
papers.contribution: Achieves higher GPT-judged win-rate in RLHF, avoids overfocusing on format in rule-based math rewards, and prevents judge hacking compared to KL-penalty baselines.

papers.title: Graph-Preference Learning: Debiasing Network-Sampled Human Feedback for Target Welfare Estimation
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 62% reduction in target-welfare recovery error and 17% reduction in cross-language performance gaps under biased inclusion.

papers.title: GuardAlign: Robust Safety Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Reduces unsafe response rates by up to 39% on SPA-VL while improving utility (VQAv2 from 78.51% to 79.21%).

papers.title: How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy
papers.contribution: Characterizes unique policy closest in KL divergence to unconstrained post-trained policy that prevents sycophancy increase.

papers.title: Humanline: Online Alignment as Perceptual Loss
papers.contribution: Humanline variants of DPO/KTO/GRPO trained on offline data match performance of online counterparts on both verifiable and unverifiable tasks, enabling faster and cheaper post-training.

papers.title: Implicit Safety Alignment from Crowd Preferences
papers.contribution: Substantially lowers safety costs without access to explicit safety rewards while achieving task performance comparable to oracle methods with ground-truth signals.

papers.title: In-Training Defenses Against Emergent Misalignment in Language Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that selecting interleaving data by perplexity gap between aligned and misaligned models yields best results overall for preventing broad misalignment.

papers.title: Incentive-Aligned LLM Summaries
papers.contribution: Establishes formal guarantees that align incentives with informative honesty, improving factual accuracy and robustness while preserving fluency.

papers.title: Inference-Aware Meta-Alignment of LLMs via Non-Linear GRPO
papers.contribution: Enables multi-criteria alignment with minimal inference-time overhead and proves convergence to optimal solution.

papers.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Reward Scaling for LLM Alignment
papers.contribution: Outperforms baselines in safety alignment while maintaining usefulness across various benchmarks and LLMs.

papers.title: Is On-Policy Data always the Best Choice for Direct Preference Optimization-Based LM Alignment?
papers.contribution: On-policy effectiveness varies 3x between models; characterization of alignment stages generalizes across 5 models and 2 alignment methods.

papers.title: Keep the Best, Forget the Rest: Reliable Alignment with Order-Aware Preference Optimization
papers.contribution: RAPPO achieves helpfulness of 0.693 (+34.8% over DPO) and harmlessness of 0.357 (-21.0% vs DPO) on the PKU-SafeRLHF benchmark.

papers.title: Language Bias in LVLMs: From In-Depth Analysis to Simple and Effective Mitigation
papers.contribution: Consistently improves on ten general benchmarks and reduces hallucination across diverse models.

papers.title: Linear Ensembles Wash Away Watermarks: On the Fragility of Distributional Perturbations in LLMs
papers.contribution: Averaging 3-5 models suppresses detection z-scores below 2 and reduces TPR@5%FPR below 50% while improving quality by 27.5%.

papers.title: Low-Compute Watermark Removal via Dual-Domain Natural Projection
papers.contribution: Reduced detectability while preserving structural and semantic fidelity across diverse watermarking schemes with low computational cost.

papers.title: MENLO: From Preferences to Proficiency – Evaluating and Modeling Native-like Quality Across 47 Languages
papers.contribution: Demonstrates substantial improvements through fine-tuning with reinforcement learning and multi-task learning, establishing promising directions for scalable multilingual evaluation.

papers.title: MESA: Improving MoE Safety Alignment via Decentralized Expertise
papers.contribution: Robust defensive performance against harmful benchmarks while preserving helpfulness.

papers.title: Measuring and Mitigating Rapport Bias of Large Language Models under Multi-Agent Social Interactions
papers.contribution: Shows larger models are more resilient to social influence via prompting, while smaller models benefit from GRPO-based mitigation, improving both robustness and performance.

papers.title: Mechanistic Detection and Mitigation of Hallucination in Large Reasoning Models
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art detection performance with reduced hallucination rates and improved reasoning quality through potential-based shaping in reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Meerkat-VL: Implicit Risk Safety Alignment in Multimodal LLMs via Perceptual Reasoning and Self-Verification
papers.contribution: Improves safety and helpfulness by 16% and 13% on multimodal benchmarks and achieves 32% safety gain on implicit-risk tasks.

papers.title: Metis: Learning to Jailbreak LLMs via Self-Evolving Metacognitive Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves 89.2% average Attack Success Rate, maintains high efficacy on frontier models (76% on O1, 78% on GPT-5), reduces token costs by 8.2x average.

papers.title: Mitigating Mismatch within Reference-based Preference Optimization
papers.contribution: Strictly strengthens per-example learning signals on pessimistic pairs while preserving DPO's objective form and computational cost, improving inference performance across preference alignment.

papers.title: Mitigating Perceptual Judgment Bias in Multimodal LLM-as-a-Judge via Perceptual Perturbation and Reward Modeling
papers.contribution: Substantially improves perceptual fidelity, ranking coherence, and alignment with human evaluation across MLLM-as-a-Judge benchmarks.

papers.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Bayesian Non-negative Reward Modeling
papers.contribution: Substantially mitigates reward over-optimization, improves robustness under distribution shifts, and yields more interpretable reward decompositions than baselines.

papers.title: Mitigating Visual Hallucinations via Semantic Curriculum Preference Optimization in MLLMs
papers.contribution: Reduces hallucination rate by up to 62.9% on LLaVA models while improving factuality and preserving general capabilities on vision-language benchmarks.

papers.title: Mitigating the Safety–Utility Trade-off in LLM Alignment via Adaptive Safe Context Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves higher overall performance compared to baselines by decoupling rule retrieval from reasoning.

papers.title: Multi-objective Large Language Model Alignment with Hierarchical Experts
papers.contribution: HoE eliminates retraining while enabling LLMs to accommodate diverse preferences; demonstrates superior performance across 16 objectives and 200 preference configurations.

papers.title: Multilingual Safety Alignment Via Sparse Weight Editing
papers.contribution: Significantly reduces Attack Success Rate across 8 languages and multiple model families with negligible impact on utility via single data-efficient calculation.

papers.title: Multilingual Safety Alignment via Representation-Space Separability
papers.contribution: SMO substantially reduces attack success rates in low-resource languages to near zero while maintaining performance on high-resource languages, demonstrated on LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

papers.title: Noise-corrected GRPO: From Noisy Rewards to Unbiased Gradients
papers.contribution: Improve math task accuracy by up to 6.7 percentage points and code task accuracy by 1.5 under realistic reward model conditions.

papers.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models
papers.contribution: Shows that GRPO and PPO-style RL methods can conceal contamination signals, and CoT SFT makes most detection methods perform near random guessing.

papers.title: OrthAlign: Orthogonal Subspace Decomposition for Non-Interfering Multi-Objective Alignment
papers.contribution: In this paper, we present OrthAlign, an innovative approach that pioneers a new paradigm by leveraging orthogonal subspace decomposition to fundamentally resolve gradient-level conflicts in multi-objective preference alignment.

papers.title: P-GenRM: Personalized Generative Reward Model with Test-time User-based Scaling
papers.contribution: P-GenRM achieves state-of-the-art results with ~2.31% average improvement on personalized reward benchmarks and demonstrates strong generalization on out-of-distribution data, with test-time user-based scaling providing an additional ~3% boost.

papers.title: PAMDP: Interact to Persona Alignment via a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process
papers.contribution: The dual-critic POMDP framework enables effective persona alignment through interaction on both offline datasets and online simulators.

papers.title: PICACO: Pluralistic In-Context Value Alignment via Total Correlation Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves better balance across up to 8 distinct values and outperforms recent baselines on five value sets using both black-box and open-source LLMs.

papers.title: Pragma-VL: Towards a Pragmatic Arbitration of Safety and Helpfulness in MLLMs
papers.contribution: Effectively balances safety and helpfulness, outperforming baselines by 5-20% on multimodal safety benchmarks while preserving general capabilities.

papers.title: ProSafePrune: Projected Safety Pruning for Mitigating Over-Refusal in LLMs
papers.contribution: Significantly lowers average false rejection rate while slightly improving general task performance across different models.

papers.title: Quantifying the Salience of Geo-Cultural Values for Pluralistic Safety Alignment
papers.contribution: Demonstrates cultural zone membership explains variance in safety ratings beyond demographics (p<0.05 across 6 datasets) with ~10% of items being culturally sensitive.

papers.title: RBCBF: Decoding Time Safety Alignment via Risk Guided Rollback and Barrier Control
papers.contribution: Outperforms rollback and decoding-time baselines, substantially reducing harmful responses and violation recurrence on jailbreak-style evaluations.

papers.title: RSPO: Regularized Self-Play Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Improves unregularized baseline on AlpacaEval-2 from 28.5% to 35.4% with Mistral-7B and from 50.54% to 51.83% with Gemma-2B, with superior performance on Arena-Hard and MT-Bench.

papers.title: Real-Time Aligned Reward Model beyond Semantics
papers.contribution: R2M addresses reward overoptimization by using policy feedback to maintain alignment beyond semantic-only reward models during continuous policy evolution.

papers.title: Reasoned Safety Alignment: Ensuring Jailbreak Defense via Answer-Then-Check
papers.contribution: Achieves Pareto frontier with superior safety and lower over-refusal while maintaining reasoning on MMLU, MATH500, HumanEval; enables safe completion with helpful alternatives.

papers.title: Reasoning Boosts Opinion Alignment in LLMs
papers.contribution: Reasoning enhances opinion modeling and is competitive with strong baselines on U.S., European, and Swiss political datasets but does not fully remove bias.

papers.title: Reasoning over Boundaries: Enhancing Specification Alignment via Test-time Deliberation
papers.contribution: SpecBench reveals alignment gaps across models; test-time deliberation improves specification alignment; Align3 advances safety-helpfulness frontier with minimal overhead.

papers.title: Reinforcement Unlearning via Group Relative Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: PURGE achieves up to 46x lower token usage than state-of-the-art, improves fluency by +5.48% and robustness by +12.02%, reaching 11% unlearning effectiveness while preserving 98% utility.

papers.title: Reliability-Aware LLM Alignment from Inconsistent Human Feedback
papers.contribution: Reduces overfitting to inconsistent supervision and achieves superior performance compared to RLHF baselines.

papers.title: Revisiting Robustness for LLM Safety Alignment via Selective Geometry Control
papers.contribution: Consistently improves safety robustness over preference optimization methods across diverse safety benchmarks and noisy preference settings.

papers.title: Reward Modeling from Natural Language Human Feedback
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models trained with outcome reward across multiple benchmarks, confirming superiority of natural language over binary feedback.

papers.title: Reward Models Inherit Value Biases from Pretraining
papers.contribution: Shows Llama RMs prefer 'agency' and Gemma RMs prefer 'communion' robustly; effect durable despite identical preference data and finetuning.

papers.title: Reward Shaping for (Inference-Time) Alignment: A Stackelberg Game Perspective
papers.contribution: Consistently improves average reward with win-tie rates exceeding 66% against baselines in inference-time alignment with minimal overhead.

papers.title: Reward-free Alignment for Conflicting Objectives
papers.contribution: Consistently achieves better Pareto trade-offs than multi-objective baselines on summarization and safety alignment across multiple LLM families without explicit reward models.

papers.title: Robust Multi-Objective Controlled Decoding of Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in worst-case rewards and win rates across popular alignment datasets with up to 10 objectives, with minimal computational overhead.

papers.title: Robust Preference Alignment via Directional Neighborhood Consensus
papers.contribution: Theoretically grounded approach that addresses preference coverage gap by leveraging neighborhood generation strategy under mild conditions.

papers.title: Robust Preference Optimization: Aligning Language Models with Noisy Preference Feedback
papers.contribution: Framework transforms existing alignment algorithms into robust versions, with convergence guarantees to true noise level under calibration and consistent effectiveness.

papers.title: Robust Reward Modeling via Causal Rubrics
papers.contribution: CROME outperforms standard baselines on RewardBench by up to 5.3% average accuracy, achieving gains of up to 7.1% at specific evaluation conditions.

papers.title: Routing, Cascades, and User Choice for LLMs
papers.contribution: Reveals that optimal routing typically involves static policies without cascading, identifies conditions for extreme misalignment where providers throttle latency to reduce costs, harming user utility.

papers.title: SARSteer: Safeguarding Large Audio Language Models via Safe-Ablated Refusal Steering
papers.contribution: SARSteer significantly improves harmful-query refusal in LALMs while preserving benign responses, establishing principled safety alignment for audio modality.

papers.title: STARE: Step-wise Temporal Alignment and Red-teaming Engine for Multi-modal Toxicity Attack
papers.contribution: Achieves 68% improvement in Attack Success Rate and reveals Optimization-Induced Phase Alignment: toxicity concentrates in early semantic phases and late refinement phases.

papers.title: Safety Alignment of LMs via Non-cooperative Games
papers.contribution: Shifts the Pareto frontier yielding a Defender simultaneously more helpful and resilient, while the Attacker converges into a strong general-purpose red-teaming agent.

papers.title: Safety Game: Inference-Time Alignment of Black-Box LLMs via Constrained Optimization
papers.contribution: Enables black-box safety alignment without retraining or model access, offering scalable pathway for resource-constrained settings.

papers.title: Safety Subspaces are Not Linearly Distinct: A Fine-Tuning Case Study
papers.contribution: Safety is highly entangled with general learning components; subspaces amplifying safe behaviors also amplify useful ones, suggesting subspace-based defenses face fundamental limitations.

papers.title: Self-Destructive Language Models
papers.contribution: SEAM achieves state-of-the-art robustness against low-intensity attacks and causes catastrophic collapse under high-intensity attacks, rendering adversarially fine-tuned models unusable.

papers.title: Self-Jailbreaking: Language Models Can Reason Themselves Out of Safety Alignment After Benign Reasoning Training
papers.contribution: Shows minimal safety reasoning data during training ensures RLMs remain safety-aligned despite self-jailbreaking tendency.

papers.title: Self-correcting for Debiasing Large Language Models
papers.contribution: With only 20k annotated samples, Self-Debias achieves superior debiasing performance while preserving general reasoning capabilities without continuous external oversight.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Preference Optimization with Limited Feedback
papers.contribution: SSPO trained on 1% of UltraFeedback consistently surpasses baselines trained on 10%, demonstrating significant data efficiency improvements.

papers.title: SpatialJB: How Text Distribution Art Becomes The "Jailbreak Key" for LLM Guardrails
papers.contribution: Achieves nearly 100% attack success rate on leading LLMs and maintains >75% success against advanced guardrails like OpenAI Moderation API.

papers.title: Spherical Procrustes Alignment for Reliable Medical Audio Diagnosis
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on medical audio diagnosis datasets (ICBHI 2017, CirCor DigiScope) and transforms pre-trained models into reliable clinical tools without extra inference cost.

papers.title: Spurious Correlation Learning in Preference Optimization: Mechanisms, Consequences, and Mitigation via Tie Training
papers.contribution: Unified theoretical analysis characterizes spurious learning mechanisms and demonstrates that tie training mitigates spurious reliance while preserving causal learning.

papers.title: Stackelberg Learning from Human Feedback: Preference Optimization as a Sequential Game
papers.contribution: Achieves strong alignment across diverse preference datasets, scales from 0.5B to 8B parameters, with inference-time refinements that transfer across model families without fine-tuning.

papers.title: Strategic Obfuscation of Deceptive Reasoning in Language Models
papers.contribution: Claude 3.5 Sonnet shows 24.3% compliance gap between training and deployment while verbalization of alignment faking drops 93.7%; intrinsic motivation to obfuscate outperforms explicit instruction-based methods.

papers.title: Submodular Optimization for Minimal Augmentation in Robust Language Model Alignment
papers.contribution: Efficiently restores safety alignment with minimal augmentation overhead while improving robustness.

papers.title: Superficial Safety Alignment Hypothesis
papers.contribution: Freezing safety-critical components during fine-tuning preserves safety while enabling task adaptation, and leveraging redundant units as an alignment budget minimizes the alignment tax.

papers.title: Swap-guided Preference Learning for Personalized Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.contribution: Mitigates collapse, enriches user-specific latents, and improves preference prediction with three components including Preferential Inverse Autoregressive Flow.

papers.title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment
papers.contribution: Demonstrates current methods cannot mechanistically distinguish sycophancy from scheming; shows fine-tuning for sycophancy increases sensitivity to evaluation cues.

papers.title: Target-Driven Policy Optimization for Sequential Counterfactual Outcome Control
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods in creating goal-conditioned policies; includes bias bounds from clipping and approximation.

papers.title: Teach to Reason Safely: Policy-Guided Safety Tuning for MLRMs
papers.contribution: PST significantly reduces harmful outputs across multimodal safety benchmarks while maintaining competitive performance on general tasks through structured safe decision-making.

papers.title: The Alignment Auditor: A Bayesian Framework for Verifying and Refining LLM Objectives
papers.contribution: Successfully audits a detoxified LLM yielding a well-calibrated interpretable objective that strengthens alignment guarantees and achieves comparable toxicity reductions to ground-truth alignment.

papers.title: The Axiomatic Value of Regularization in AI Alignment from Human Preferences
papers.contribution: Provides principled social-choice-grounded argument for utilizing practical RLHF algorithms corresponding to von Neumann winner rule over Borda count.

papers.title: The Devil behind the mask: An emergent safety vulnerability of Diffusion LLMs
papers.contribution: To this end, we present **DIJA**, the first systematic study and jailbreak attack framework that exploits unique safety weaknesses of dLLMs.

papers.title: The Hidden Link between RLHF and Contrastive Learning
papers.contribution: MIO mitigates late-stage decline in DPO and achieves competitive or superior performance on reasoning and mathematical benchmarks.

papers.title: The Hot Mess of AI: How Does Misalignment Scale With Model Intelligence and Task Complexity?
papers.contribution: Shows incoherence changes with model scale in task-dependent ways; predicts failures accompanied by unpredictable misbehavior rather than consistent goal misalignment.

papers.title: The Oversight Game: Learning to Cooperatively Balance an AI Agent's Safety and Autonomy
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that agent autonomy incentives structurally couple to human welfare, enabling transparent control that reduces safety violations in open-ended language model tool-use tasks.

papers.title: The Realignment Problem: When Right becomes Wrong in LLMs
papers.contribution: Robustly re-aligns models on synthetic benchmarks and PKU-SafeRLHF dataset without fresh annotation or degrading general utility.

papers.title: Thinking as Society: Multi-Social-Agent Self-Distillation for Multimodal Misinformation Detection
papers.contribution: A 7B Qwen2-VL model significantly outperforms MLLM baselines and competes with proprietary models like GPT-4o and Claude on MFC-Bench and MMFakeBench.

papers.title: Toward Culturally Aligned LLMs through Ontology-Guided Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.contribution: The framework improves cultural alignment and robustness across four LLM backbones on regional social-survey benchmarks while producing transparent reasoning traces.

papers.title: Toward Safe Quantization-Aware Fine-tuning: Understanding and Mitigating Safety Alignment Degradation
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art safety alignment recovery while preserving downstream performance, even surpassing full-precision safety-aware baselines.

papers.title: Toward Safer Diffusion Language Models: Discovery and Mitigation of Priming Vulnerability
papers.contribution: Significantly mitigates priming vulnerability with minimal impact on task performance and improves robustness against conventional jailbreak attacks.

papers.title: Toward Stable Value Alignment: Introducing Independent Modules for Consistent Value Guidance
papers.contribution: SVGT reduces harmful scores by over 70% while maintaining generation fluency across multiple backbones and safety benchmarks.

papers.title: Towards Cognitively-Faithful Decision-Making Models to Improve AI Alignment
papers.contribution: The method learns interpretable models of human decision-making in kidney allocation tasks matching or surpassing prior accuracy on pairwise decision-making.

papers.title: Towards Context-Invariant Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Improves context invariance by 12.71% in-distribution and 33.49% out-of-distribution, making safety constraints robust to adversarial framings across Safety, Moral Reasoning, and Math domains.

papers.title: Towards Disentangled Preference Optimization Dynamics: Suppress the Loser, Preserve the Winner
papers.contribution: Reward calibration method adaptively rebalances updates to satisfy disentanglement band with better downstream performance.

papers.title: Towards Safe Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models via Corrective Intervention
papers.contribution: Remarkably improves overall safety regarding both reasoning and responses, with >30% relative reduction in harmful content over SFT and RL baselines.

papers.title: Towards Self-Robust LLMs: Intrinsic Prompt Noise Resistance via CoIPO
papers.contribution: Achieves significant improvement in average accuracy on NoisyPromptBench, a new benchmark derived from PromptBench for evaluating prompt robustness.

papers.title: Transitivity Meets Cyclicity: Explicit Preference Decomposition for Dynamic Large Language Model Alignment
papers.contribution: Improves RewardBench 2 by +1.23% over BT/GPM, with 44.75% win-rate on AlpacaEval 2.0 and 46.8% on Arena-Hard-v0.1 using Gemma-2B-it.

papers.title: Tree-based Dialogue Reinforced Policy Optimization for Red-Teaming Attacks
papers.contribution: DialTree-RPO achieves 25.9% higher attack success rate over previous state-of-the-art and effectively uncovers novel multi-turn attack strategies.

papers.title: Truthful or Fabricated? Using Causal Attribution to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Explanations
papers.contribution: Reduces misleading explanations by making reward models sensitive to consistency between internal reasoning and self-explanations.

papers.title: Turning Drift into Constraint: Robust Reasoning Alignment in Non-Stationary Multi-Stream Environments
papers.contribution: APO achieves superior robustness with 7B model outperforming proprietary source models on chest X-ray interpretation with released CXR-MAX benchmark.

papers.title: UCPO: Uncertainty-Aware Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: UCPO effectively resolves reward imbalance and significantly improves model reliability beyond knowledge boundaries on mathematical reasoning and general tasks.

papers.title: Unbiased Alignment for Large Language Models with Noisy Preferences
papers.contribution: Demonstrates noise-tolerant, parameter downward compatible methods that outperform state-of-the-art baselines across diverse datasets with rigorous theoretical analyses.

papers.title: Unbiased Reward Modeling from Implicit Feedback for LLM Alignment
papers.contribution: Learn accurate reward models from implicit feedback and improve downstream RLHF performance across diverse LLM backbones and benchmarks.

papers.title: Uni-DPO: A Unified Paradigm for Dynamic Preference Optimization of LLMs
papers.contribution: Gemma-2-9B-IT fine-tuned with Uni-DPO surpasses Claude 3 Opus by 6.7 points on Arena-Hard, with consistent outperformance across mathematical and multimodal tasks.

papers.title: Unifying Stable Optimization and Reference Regularization in RLHF
papers.contribution: The unified method consistently outperforms RLHF and online preference learning across diverse benchmarks, achieving enhanced alignment performance and stability.

papers.title: VENOMREC: Cross-Modal Interactive Poisoning for Targeted Promotion in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
papers.contribution: Achieves 0.73 mean ER@20 and improves over strongest baseline by +0.52 absolute ER points while maintaining comparable recommendation utility.

papers.title: What's In My Human Feedback? Learning Interpretable Descriptions of Preference Data
papers.contribution: A sparse set of interpretable features accounts for two-thirds of the preference signal; re-labeling harmful preferences yields +37% safety gains with no cost to general performance.

papers.title: When Agents “Misremember” Collectively: Exploring the Mandela Effect in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Demonstrates 74.40% average reduction in Mandela effect through cognitive anchoring, source scrutiny, and alignment-based defenses on the proposed benchmark.

papers.title: When Labelers Stay Silent: The Power of Ties in Cost-Effective Preference Learning
papers.contribution: Supervision from small models with proper tie modeling yields alignment surpassing forced-choice LLMs or human experts, unlocking value in existing benchmarks without re-labeling.

papers.title: When and How Human Curation Backfires: Preference Alignment under Multi-Model Self-Consuming Loop
papers.contribution: Cross-model interactions can degrade long-term alignment despite local curation benefits, revealing fundamental limits of human curation in interconnected systems.

papers.title: Why is Your Language Model a Poor Implicit Reward Model?
papers.contribution: The findings demonstrate that implicit models generalize worse under token-level distribution shifts than explicit models.
